key_insight: Brain growth charts from MRI can turn complex leukodystrophy scans into age-adjusted centile scores that reveal shared and disease-specific white-matter/brain volume patterns.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help distinguish leukodystrophy subtypes, quantify severity, and support biomarker development for trial readiness.
method: 434 MRI sessions from 274 genetically confirmed pediatric leukodystrophy patients were analyzed across 6 disorders.
Deep-learning segmentation derived global and regional brain volumes from clinical MRI.
Normative models were built from 7,628 control scans using generalized additive models, then patient centiles were calculated versus typical development.
evidence_signal: The study used a large multicenter patient cohort with a very large pediatric control dataset to compare centile deviations across leukodystrophy subtypes.
watch_item: This is a retrospective cross-sectional imaging study, so biomarker performance still needs prospective validation before routine use.
paper_title: Normative modeling for quantitative brain MRI phenotyping and biomarker discovery for pediatric leukodystrophies
